To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a new tissue source of fetal MSCs, which can be used to derive pure cultures of fetal and maternal MSCs from one tissue.

we have demonstrated the existence of both maternal and fetal mesenchymalmal stromal cells in the terminal chorionic villus (TCV) tissue of the term placenta, which can be isolated by a simple and efficient methodology and propagated as pure cultures in vitro.

we have shown for the first time that the tips of terminal villi of human placenta contain fetal and maternal cells, and that we have established pure cultures of both fetal and maternal meso-enchymal stem cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the derivation of pure fetal MSCs from the TCV of normal human term placentae.
understanding how MSCs from adult and fetal tissue sources differ in their genetic and epigenomic profiles, and how these differences impact on their regenerative potential in vivo.
the development of new methodologies for the derivation of human MSCs and their applications in tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.

the MSC from TCV can be propagated in vitro in long term, and the purity of these MSCs can be confirmed by the FISH and STR genotyping.
we have shown the presence of fetal cells within the tips and the maternal cells in the base of TCV.

we have demonstrated the existence of fetal and maternal mesodermal cells within the tips (terminal chorionic villi) of human term placental villi, and we have developed a novel and robust methodology to establish pure cultures of fetal and maternal MSC from this source.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the feasibility of establishing pure fetal MSC cultures in vitro from a readily available source of fetal cells, and have also shown the presence of maternal cells within the TCV of normal human term placentae, and their potential use in regenerative medicine.
we have developed an efficient method for the propagation of pure fetal MSCs from human term placenta which will be of great value for the field of regenerative medicine.

we have demonstrated the existence of fetal and maternal MSCs in the TCV tips of normal human term placentae and have developed a novel and robust protocol to isolate pure fetal and maternal MSC cultures from them, which will have significant implications for the field of regenerative medicine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TCV of the placenta provides a unique tissue source to obtain pure fetal MSCs, which can be used for therapeutic applications.
the tips of terminal villi from human term placenta contain pure fetal and maternal cells, which can be easily isolated and propagated to obtain pure cultures of fetal and maternal MSCs.
we have shown that the tips of TCV of human placenta can be used as a source of pure fetal MSCs and also pure maternal MSCs.
